source.title: Some open problems in the theory of infinite dimensional algebras

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a finitely presented infinite torsion group, where a torsion group means a group in which every element has finite order?

evidence.quote: let G be a finitely generated torsion group, that is, for an arbitrary element g in G there exists n = n(g) > 1, such that g n = 1.
Problem 1. Do there exist infinite finitely presented torsion groups?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a field and let A be a finitely presented K-algebra. Suppose A is algebraic, meaning that for every element a in A there is a polynomial f_a(t) in K[t] with f_a(a) = 0; in the nil case, all such polynomials may be taken to be powers of t. Must every such finitely presented algebraic, and in particular nil, K-algebra be finite-dimensional over K?

evidence.quote: Let K be a field and let A be a finitely generated K-algebra, which is algebraic, that is, for an arbitrary element a in A there exists a polynomial fa(t) in K[t] such that fa(a) = 0.
Problem 2. Is it true that every finitely presented algebraic (nil) algebra is finite dimensional?

accepted.question_text: Let A = A_1 + A_2 + ... be a graded algebra with A_i A_j contained in A_{i+j} and finite-dimensional homogeneous pieces. Suppose A is quadratic: it is generated by A_1 and has defining relators that are homogeneous of degree two, of the form sum alpha_ij x_i x_j = 0. If A is a nil algebra, must A be nilpotent?

evidence.quote: We say that the algebra A is quadratic ... if it is generated by A1 and presented ... by relators which all look as sum alphaij xi xj = 0.
Problem 3. Is it true that a quadratic nil algebra is nilpotent?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a finitely generated associative algebra A over a field K that is infinite-dimensional, is nil, and has finite Gelfand-Kirillov dimension, where finite Gelfand-Kirillov dimension means polynomial growth of the dimensions of the subspaces S^n spanned by products of length at most n from a finite-dimensional generating subspace S?
accepted.context_brief: Nil algebras of finite GK dimension

evidence.quote: The algebra A has a finite Gelfand-Kirillov dimension (or a polynomial growth) if there exists a polynomial f(t) such that dimK S n <= f(n) for all n > 1.
Problem 4. (L. Small). Does there exist an infinite dimensional nil algebra of finite GK-dimension?

accepted.question_text: Let A be a Golod-Shafarevich algebra: a graded algebra A = <X | R = 0> over a field K, where X has m degree-one generators, R is a graded relator subspace in degrees at least two with Hilbert series H_R(t), and there exists a number t_0 in (0,1) such that H_R(t) converges at t_0 and 1 - m t_0 + H_R(t_0) < 0. Must every such Golod-Shafarevich algebra have a homomorphic image that is both infinite-dimensional and of finite Gelfand-Kirillov dimension?
accepted.context_brief: GS algebras and finite GK images

evidence.quote: If A has such a presentation then we say that A is a GS-algebra.
Problem 5. Is it true that an arbitrary GS-algebra has an infinite dimensional homomorphic image of finite GK-dimension?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a field of characteristic p > 0 and let T = K[t_0, t_1, ... | t_i^p = 0 for i >= 0] be the polynomial algebra in countably many truncated variables. Write partial_i = d/dt_i. For n >= 1 define v_n = partial_n + sum_{i=n+1}^infty (t_0 ... t_{i-2})^{p-1} partial_i, as in the self-similar Lie algebra construction described by Petrogradsky, Shestakov, and Zelmanov. Let A be the associative subalgebra of End_K(T) generated by v_1 and v_2. Is A a nil algebra?

evidence.quote: Let K be a field of characteristic p > 0; T = K[t0, t1, ... | ti p = 0, i > 0] is the polynomial algebra in countably many truncated variables.
Let A be the associative subalgebra of Endk T generated by v1, v2. Problem 6. Is A a nil algebra?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a division algebra that is finitely generated, algebraic, and infinite-dimensional?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Do there exist infinite dimensional finitely generated algebraic division algebras?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a division algebra that is finitely generated and infinite-dimensional, even without requiring it to be algebraic?

evidence.quote: Even a weaker version of this question is still open. Problem 8. Do there exist infinite dimensional finitely generated division algebras?

accepted.question_text: Using the same Lie algebra generated by v_1 and v_2 from the self-similar derivation construction over the truncated polynomial algebra T, let U be its universal associative enveloping algebra and let Z be the center of U. Because powers of elements of the Lie algebra fall into Z, form the ring of fractions D = (Z \ {0})^{-1} U. Is D an algebraic division algebra?
accepted.context_brief: Fraction division algebra from enveloping algebra

evidence.quote: Let U be the universal associative enveloping algebra of Lie <v1, v2>. Let Z be the center of U.
Consider the ring of fractions D = (Z r {0})-1 U. Problem 9. Is D an algebraic division algebra?

accepted.question_text: Let p and q be distinct primes, let K_p = Z/pZ and K_q = Z/qZ, and let SL_1(n, K_p[t]) for n > 3 be the congruence subgroup of the special linear group over the polynomial ring K_p[t] used in the source. Does the group algebra K_q[SL_1(n, K_p[t])] satisfy algebraic property tau, where property tau for a residually finite associative K-algebra A generated by a finite-dimensional space S means that there is an epsilon > 0 such that every infinite-dimensional residually finite A-module V with no nonzero finite-dimensional submodules satisfies dim(W + S W) > (1 + epsilon) dim W for every finite-dimensional subspace W of V?
accepted.context_brief: Finite-field group algebras and property tau

evidence.quote: A residually finite associative K-algebra A generated by a finite dimensional space S satisfies the property tau if there exists epsilon > 0 such that ... dim(W + SW) > (1 + epsilon) dim W.
Problem 10. Let p and q be distinct primes. Does the group algebra Kq[SL1(n, Kp[t])], n > 3 satisfy property tau?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a field of characteristic zero. Does the group algebra K[SL(3, Z)] satisfy algebraic property tau in the sense that some finite-dimensional generating subspace S expands every finite-dimensional subspace W of every infinite-dimensional residually finite K[SL(3,Z)]-module with no nonzero finite-dimensional submodules by a uniform factor greater than 1?
accepted.context_brief: SL(3,Z) group algebra and property tau

evidence.quote: We even don't know an answer to the following question. Problem 11. Let K be a field of zero characteristic. Does the group algebra K[SL(3, Z)] satisfy tau?

accepted.question_text: Does every lattice in SL(2,C) fail to have group property tau, where property tau means that, for a fixed finite generating set, the Cayley graphs of all finite quotients form a uniform expander family?

evidence.quote: a group G generated by a finite set S has property (tau) if there exists epsilon > 0 such that for every homomorphism onto a finite group G0 ... Cay(G0, S0) is an epsilon-expander.
Conjecture 1. (A. Lubotzky-P. Sarnak, [29]) A lattice in SL(2, C) does not have property tau.

accepted.question_text: Is every irreducible compact three-dimensional hyperbolic manifold virtually Haken, meaning that it has a finite-sheeted cover that is Haken; equivalently, does every cocompact lattice Gamma in SL(2,C) have a finite-index subgroup that is either a free product with amalgamation or an HNN construction?

evidence.quote: The Virtual Haken Conjecture. Every irreducible compact 3-dimensional hyperbolic manifold has a finite sheeted cover which is Haken, or, equivalently, every cocompact lattice Gamma in SL(2, C) has a finite index subgroup which is either a free product with amalgam, or an HNN-construction.

accepted.question_text: Does every Golod-Shafarevich algebra fail to have algebraic property tau?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. A GS-algebra does not have tau.
If A has such a presentation then we say that A is a GS-algebra.

accepted.question_text: Let A = A_1 + A_2 + ... be a graded algebra generated by A_1 with dim A_1 = m, and suppose A is presented by fewer than m^2/4 generic quadratic relators. For the Veronese subalgebras A^(n) = A_n + A_{2n} + A_{3n} + ..., is it true that all but finitely many A^(n) admit an epimorphism onto the polynomial algebra K[t]?
accepted.context_brief: Generic quadratic algebras and Veronese subalgebras

evidence.quote: By a Veronese subalgebra A(n) of A we mean A(n) = An + A2n + A3n + ...

Conjecture 3. Let A = A1 + A2 + ... be a graded algebra generated by A1, dim A1 = m and presented by < m2/4 generic quadratic relators. Then all but finitely many Veronese subalgebras can be epimorphically mapped onto the polynomial algebra K[t].

needs_review.question_text_raw: The Grigorchuk groups are of particular interest since they are of intermediate growth: the sequence |S1| < |S2| < ... grows faster than any polynomial but slower than any exponential function. Is there an analog for algebras?

evidence.quote: The Grigorchuk groups are of particular interest since they are of intermediate growth ... Is there an analog for algebras?

trace.notes: Normalized the input as a zbMATH bibliographic resolver URL with trailing identifier 5238275.

Local shard metadata identified the exact work as Efim Zelmanov, Some open problems in the theory of infinite dimensional algebras, Journal of the Korean Mathematical Society 44(5), 1185-1195, 2007, DOI 10.4134/JKMS.2007.44.5.1185. Metadata was used only for identity and recovery.

The zbMATH page and API were treated as metadata resolvers. The KCI landing page exposed bibliographic metadata and references, while the paperzz mirror exposed readable full text for the exact title and journal pages. The paperzz mirror was selected as the primary readable HTML artifact.

Mapped sections: I The Burnside and Kurosh problems; II The Golod-Shafarevich construction; III Growth and GK-dimension; IV Self-similar Lie algebras; V Property tau and dimension expanders; VI Golod-Shafarevich construction and property tau. Key definitions included torsion group, algebraic and nil algebra, quadratic algebra, Veronese subalgebra, GS group/algebra, GK dimension, the derivation algebra construction, dimension expander, and property tau.

Extracted Problems 4-5 from the growth and GK-dimension section.

Extracted Problems 6-9 from the self-similar Lie algebras section. Also flagged the broad Grigorchuk-analogue question for review because the target algebraic analogue was not specified precisely enough.
Extracted Problems 10-11 from the property tau and dimension expanders section.
Extracted the Virtual Haken Conjecture and Conjectures 1-3 from the Golod-Shafarevich construction and property tau section.

Expanded the construction of T, the derivations, and the associative algebra A generated by v1 and v2.
Kept the division-algebra problem close to the source wording to avoid unsupported assumptions about the base field.
Stated the weaker division-algebra question separately from the algebraic version.
